title: The second supplement to quadratic reciprocity, the Zolotarev way: J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8)
description: A direct payoff of the full odd-modulus Zolotarev–Frobenius identity (the parent), answering the a = 2 half of its listed open question #3: 'Recover the supplementary laws (a = -1 and a = 2) for odd n as values of signRingHom.' This is the sibling of the first supplement (a = -1); here we deliver the SECOND supplement, a = 2: for every odd n > 0, J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8), and we identify it as the sign of the DOUBLING permutation x ↦ 2·x on ℤ/n (the Zolotarev permutation of the unit 2). Honest comparison with the first supplement: negation x ↦ -x is an involution, so its sign was read off by a self-contained fixed-point parity count; doubling x ↦ 2·x is NOT an involution, so an independent evaluation of its sign would amount to reproving Gauss's lemma for the prime 2. We therefore route through the parent identity sign(ringMulPerm 2) = J(2 | n) (which already encapsulates Gauss's lemma) and Mathlib's jacobiSym.at_two (J(2 | b) = χ₈ b). The genuinely NEW mathematical content is the closed-form POWER formula for the octic character χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) for odd n — which Mathlib does NOT provide (it offers only the mod-8 case split χ₈_nat_eq_if_mod_eight). Establishing this power form is a clean parity computation: for odd n = 2m+1, (n²-1)/8 = m(m+1)/2 is the m-th triangular number, whose parity is governed by m mod 4 ↔ n mod 8 (n ≡ ±1 mod 8 ⇒ even ⇒ +1; n ≡ ±3 mod 8 ⇒ odd ⇒ -1). The entry records the Jacobi-symbol supplement, the doubling-permutation sign in unit and canonical forms, and the Legendre/Euler-criterion special case (2 / p) = (-1)^((p²-1)/8).

overview.text: Zolotarev's theory reads arithmetic symbols as permutation parities. The parent established the dictionary in full generality — sign(x ↦ a·x on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for all odd n — and the supplementary laws are the dictionary entries for special a. For a = -1 the permutation is negation, an involution whose parity is a fixed-point count (the sibling entry). For a = 2 the permutation is doubling x ↦ 2·x, which is not an involution: its cycle structure is governed by the multiplicative order of 2 mod n, so there is no comparably cheap independent parity count. This entry therefore reads the second supplement off the parent's identity together with Mathlib's jacobiSym.at_two (J(2 | n) = χ₈ n), and supplies the missing analytic ingredient as a clean combinatorial fact: the closed-form power expression χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8). The exponent (n²-1)/8 equals, for odd n = 2m+1, the triangular number m(m+1)/2; its parity is determined by m mod 4, equivalently n mod 8, giving +1 at n ≡ ±1 (mod 8) and -1 at n ≡ ±3 (mod 8). Combining, J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) and the doubling permutation x ↦ 2·x on ℤ/n has exactly this sign.
overview.historicalContext: The second supplementary law (2/p) = (-1)^((p²-1)/8) — equivalently, 2 is a quadratic residue mod an odd prime p iff p ≡ ±1 (mod 8) — was first proved by Gauss, classically via Gauss's lemma (counting how many of 2·1, 2·2, …, 2·(p-1)/2 exceed p/2). Its Jacobi-symbol form J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) extends it to all odd n. Zolotarev (1872) reorganized quadratic reciprocity around permutation signs, with the Legendre symbol as the sign of a multiplication permutation; Frobenius (1914) generalized this to the Jacobi symbol on composite moduli. In that picture the supplements are the permutation parities at a = -1 and a = 2; the present entry records the second of these as the sign of the doubling permutation, the value supplied by the octic character χ₈.
overview.problemStatement: Open question #3 of elementary-quadratic-reciprocity-oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01, and explicitly the first listed open question of the first-supplement sibling: 'Prove the SECOND supplement J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) the same way, by computing the sign of the doubling permutation x ↦ 2x on ℤ/n.' This entry answers it: for every odd n > 0, J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8), and that value is the sign of the Zolotarev doubling permutation.
overview.proofStrategy: exponent_parity: for odd n, ((n²-1)/8) % 2 = (n mod 8 ∈ {1,7} ? 0 : 1). Write n = 2m+1; then (2m+1)²-1 = 4·m(m+1), so (n²-1)/8 = m(m+1)/2 (proved by omega from the ring identity (2m+1)² = 4·m(m+1)+1). Decompose m = 4j+s with s < 4 (interval_cases); in each residue class rewrite the product m(m+1) by a ring identity 2·(8j²+…) and discharge the parity and the n-mod-8 side condition with split_ifs + omega. neg_one_pow_exponent: convert exponent_parity into (-1)^((n²-1)/8) = (n mod 8 ∈ {1,7} ? 1 : -1) using Even.neg_one_pow / Odd.neg_one_pow. chi8_eq_neg_one_pow: χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) by rewriting χ₈ via ZMod.χ₈_nat_eq_if_mod_eight and matching the two case splits (the n even branch is killed by oddness). jacobiSym_two: J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) by jacobiSym.at_two then chi8_eq_neg_one_pow. sign_ringMulPerm_two / sign_doubling: the parent's sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_odd (unit u with residue 2, integer representative 2) gives sign(ringMulPerm u) = J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8); the canonical form uses ZMod.unitOfCoprime 2 with Nat.Coprime 2 n from oddness. legendreSym_two: the prime case (2 / p) = (-1)^((p²-1)/8) via jacobiSym.legendreSym.to_jacobiSym and Nat.Prime.odd_of_ne_two.
keyInsights: Unlike the first supplement, the doubling permutation x ↦ 2·x is not an involution, so its sign cannot be obtained by a fixed-point count; an independent evaluation would reprove Gauss's lemma for 2. Routing through the parent identity (which already contains Gauss's lemma) and Mathlib's jacobiSym.at_two is the honest tractable path — and the genuinely new piece is the χ₈ power formula it leaves to be supplied.

Mathlib has the octic character χ₈ only in mod-8 case-split form (χ₈_nat_eq_if_mod_eight); the closed-form power expression χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) — the octic analogue of ZMod.χ₄_eq_neg_one_pow — is not in the library, and is the reusable contribution of this entry.

The exponent unwinds to a triangular number: for odd n = 2m+1, (n²-1)/8 = m(m+1)/2 = T_m. The parity of T_m has period 4 in m (T_m even iff m ≡ 0 or 3 mod 4), which matches n mod 8: even exponent ⇔ n ≡ ±1 (mod 8) ⇔ χ₈ n = +1.

The whole parity computation is reduced to omega after one ring identity per residue class: m(m+1) is rewritten as 2·(quadratic in j) so that the division by 2 and the subsequent mod 2 become linear, and split_ifs resolves the disjunctive n-mod-8 side condition that omega cannot case-split on its own.

Oddness of n enters at two compatible places: it makes 2 a unit mod n (so the doubling permutation and the unit ℤ/n)ˣ representative exist) and it kills the n-even branch of χ₈ — exactly the modulus on which the Jacobi symbol J(2 | ·) is undefined.
prerequisites: The full odd-modulus Zolotarev–Frobenius identity ZolotarevFullOdd.sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_odd (the parent) and the whole-ring multiplication permutation ZolotarevCRT.ringMulPerm
Mathlib's Jacobi-symbol value at 2: jacobiSym.at_two (J(2 | b) = χ₈ b) and the octic character ZMod.χ₈ with ZMod.χ₈_nat_eq_if_mod_eight
Even.neg_one_pow / Odd.neg_one_pow for ℤ, and Nat parity/division reasoning discharged by omega
Units of ℤ/n: ZMod.unitOfCoprime and ZMod.coe_unitOfCoprime, with Nat.Coprime 2 n from Odd n (Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd, Nat.two_dvd_ne_zero, Nat.odd_iff)
For the prime case: jacobiSym.legendreSym.to_jacobiSym and Nat.Prime.odd_of_ne_two

sections.title: Overview: The Second Supplement (a = 2), the Zolotarev Way
sections.summary: Module docstring, parent import (ElementaryQuadraticReciprocityOQ01OQ03OQ01OQ01OQ01OQ01OQ01), and setup (namespace ZolotarevSecondSupplement; open Equiv.Perm; ringMulPerm from ZolotarevCRT; variable {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]). This entry delivers the SECOND supplement to quadratic reciprocity, J(2|n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) for odd n>0, and identifies it as the sign of the doubling permutation x ↦ 2x on ℤ/n. Unlike the a=-1 first supplement (negation is an involution, allowing a Gauss-free fixed-point parity count), doubling is not an involution, so the proof routes through the parent identity sign(ringMulPerm 2) = J(2|n) and Mathlib's jacobiSym.at_two. The genuinely new content is the closed-form power formula χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) (Mathlib provides only the mod-8 case split), proved via the triangular-number identity (n²-1)/8 = m(m+1)/2 and the parity fact exponent_parity. Content (0 sorries, 0 axioms): exponent_parity, neg_one_pow_exponent, chi8_eq_neg_one_pow, jacobiSym_two, sign_ringMulPerm_two, sign_doubling, legendreSym_two.
sections.mathContext: Zolotarev's 1872 insight recasts the Legendre/Jacobi symbol as the sign of a permutation on ℤ/n; here the unit 2 gives the doubling permutation whose sign is the second supplement — completing the dictionary between permutation signs and the full Jacobi symbol in the spirit of Frobenius (1914).

sections.title: Parity of the supplement exponent
sections.content: exponent_parity: for odd n, ((n²-1)/8) % 2 = (if n % 8 = 1 ∨ n % 8 = 7 then 0 else 1). With n = 2m+1, (n²-1)/8 = m(m+1)/2 = T_m (the m-th triangular number), proved by omega from (2m+1)² = 4·m(m+1)+1. Decomposing m = 4j+s and rewriting m(m+1) = 2·(8j²+…) per residue, split_ifs + omega finish both the exponent parity and the n-mod-8 side condition.

sections.title: The supplement value as a signed power
sections.content: neg_one_pow_exponent: (-1)^((n²-1)/8) = (if n % 8 = 1 ∨ n % 8 = 7 then 1 else -1), obtained from exponent_parity via Even.neg_one_pow / Odd.neg_one_pow: +1 when n ≡ ±1 (mod 8), -1 when n ≡ ±3 (mod 8).

sections.title: Closed-form power formula for χ₈
sections.content: chi8_eq_neg_one_pow: χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) for odd n — the octic analogue of ZMod.χ₄_eq_neg_one_pow, absent from Mathlib (which has only the case split χ₈_nat_eq_if_mod_eight). Proved by rewriting χ₈ via the case split and matching it to neg_one_pow_exponent, the n-even branch being killed by oddness.

sections.title: The second supplement and the doubling permutation
sections.content: jacobiSym_two: J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) by jacobiSym.at_two (J(2 | n) = χ₈ n) and chi8_eq_neg_one_pow. sign_ringMulPerm_two / sign_doubling: the parent's sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_odd gives sign(x ↦ 2·x on ℤ/n) = J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8), in a unit-hypothesis form and a canonical hypothesis-free form using ZMod.unitOfCoprime 2. legendreSym_two: the Legendre/Euler-criterion case (2 / p) = (-1)^((p²-1)/8) at an odd prime.

meta.author: Gauss (second supplement); Zolotarev (1872), Frobenius (1914) (permutation-sign route)
meta.assumptions: None. The file has 0 axiom declarations, 0 sorries, no native_decide, and no assumption-carrying structures. The headline theorems chi8_eq_neg_one_pow, jacobiSym_two, sign_doubling and legendreSym_two were checked with #print axioms and depend only on propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound (the standard foundational axioms, which do not count as assumptions). The value J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) is classical and reachable in Mathlib via jacobiSym.at_two + the χ₈ case split; the contributions here are (i) the explicit power formula χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8), which Mathlib does not provide, and (ii) the reading of the second supplement as the sign of Zolotarev's doubling permutation. The sign value is honestly routed through J(2 | n) = χ₈ n rather than an independent inversion count (which would reprove Gauss's lemma for 2).

conclusion.summary: Proves, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, the second supplementary law of quadratic reciprocity J(2 | n) = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) for every odd n > 0, and identifies it as the sign of the doubling permutation x ↦ 2·x on ℤ/n via the parent's full odd-modulus Zolotarev–Frobenius identity. The new analytic ingredient is the closed-form power formula for the octic character, χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) — absent from Mathlib, which carries χ₈ only as a mod-8 case split — proved by recognizing (n²-1)/8 as the triangular number m(m+1)/2 (for n = 2m+1) and computing its parity from m mod 4 ↔ n mod 8. Also records the Legendre/Euler-criterion specialization (2 / p) = (-1)^((p²-1)/8).
conclusion.implications: Completes the a = 2 half of the parent's open question — and the explicit follow-up flagged by the first-supplement sibling — so that both supplementary laws are now recorded as Zolotarev permutation parities, with the main reciprocity law (the two-dimensional shuffle) the only remaining piece for a fully self-contained Zolotarev proof of quadratic reciprocity in the gallery. The reusable nugget is chi8_eq_neg_one_pow: the octic character in explicit power form, the χ₈ counterpart of ZMod.χ₄_eq_neg_one_pow, suitable for upstreaming to Mathlib.
openQuestions: Give a genuinely independent permutation-theoretic evaluation of the doubling sign sign(x ↦ 2x on ℤ/n) — e.g. via the cycle structure governed by the multiplicative order of 2 mod n, or a direct inversion count — so the second supplement is read off the permutation without routing through χ₈, matching the self-contained style of the first supplement.
Upstream χ₈ n = (-1)^((n²-1)/8) (for odd n) to Mathlib as the octic analogue of ZMod.χ₄_eq_neg_one_pow, completing the power-form characterizations of the small quadratic/quartic/octic characters.
Combine the two supplements with the main reciprocity law to assemble a fully self-contained Zolotarev proof of quadratic reciprocity in the gallery.
